verses.text: The LORD says, “Keep justice going and do what's right. My salvation is close, and my righteousness is about to be revealed.
Blessed is anyone who does this and sticks to it, who keeps the Sabbath holy and keeps their hands from doing anything evil.”
A foreigner who's joined the LORD shouldn't say, “The LORD will cut me off from his people.” A eunuch shouldn't say, “Look at me, I'm a dried-up tree.”
The LORD says, “To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, choose what makes me glad, and hold tight to my covenant,
I'll give them a memorial and a name inside my house and within my walls that's better than sons and daughters. I'll give them a name that lasts forever and won't be cut off.
And the foreigners who join the LORD to serve him and love his name, everyone who keeps from profaning the Sabbath and holds fast to my covenant,

I'll bring them to my holy mountain and make them glad in my house of prayer. I'll accept their burnt offerings and sacrifices on my altar. My house will be called a house of prayer for every people.”
The Lord GOD, who gathers Israel's outcasts, says, “I'll gather still more people to them, along with those I've already gathered.”
Come and devour, all you animals out in the fields and all you animals in the forest!
Israel's watchmen are blind. None of them knows what's going on. They're dogs that can't bark. They lie around dreaming and love to sleep.
Those dogs are greedy and never have enough. They're shepherds who don't understand. They've all gone their own way, each looking out for what they can get.
“Come on,” they say. “I'll get the wine, and we'll drink our fill of strong liquor! Tomorrow will be just like today, only even bigger.”
